text:
alex: FYI hit a weird `redwoodctl` install conflict when switching between brew and the tarball. `which redwoodctl` shows /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl but `redwoodctl --version` prints the tarball build (different build id).

sam: that usually means a stale symlink left behind. did you run `brew unlink redwoodctl` or `brew uninstall`? brew sometimes leaves shims in /usr/local/bin.

alex: i did `brew uninstall` but the old binary stayed. removing the file fixed it, but curious if installer should warn.

tara: installer does try to avoid clobbering but we focused on fresh installs. edge case: if PATH has /usr/local/bin before /opt/homebrew/bin and a stale file exists, new installer might write to ~/bin while CLI picks the old one. we should validate on startup and warn if versions mismatch.

alex: also saw `Permission denied` when I let the installer add `~/.local/bin` to PATH in .bashrc because my dotfiles are read-only. installer failed silently.

sam: workaround: print a clear message: "unable to persist PATH update, please add ~/.local/bin to your shell manually". filed DX-700.

install-bot: created patch branch installer/validate-path-versions - adds startup diagnostic comparing `redwoodctl --version` to installed metadata (PR #2301).

tara: another UX nit: `redwoodctl upgrade` should detect multiple installs and offer to remove the old one. adding that to DX-701.

alex: tiny helpful command I used: `command -v redwoodctl && redwoodctl --version || echo 'not installed'` to find the mismatch. saving this in our onboarding checklist.

devex-bot: note added to devex/cli/install.md: PATH conflict troubleshooting, manual PATH update instructions, and example commands.
